stem: The Spark UI shows one task in a groupBy stage reading 50 GB of shuffle data while the median task reads 2 GB. Adaptive Query Execution is on and the stage is an aggregation, not a join. The fix must spread that one hot key over more tasks, and the cluster itself is otherwise healthy.

option_texts.A: Salt the hot key so it spreads over more tasks, then merge the partial results
option_texts.B: Raise executor memory so that the single long task has enough room to finish sooner
option_texts.C: Lower spark.sql.shuffle.partitions so that the stage performs fewer and larger shuffle reads
option_texts.D: Turn Adaptive Query Execution off so that the aggregation runs as a broadcast instead

drill_answer_short: AQE splits skewed tasks only for sort merge join and shuffle hash join, so a skewed aggregation needs salting
decision_hinge: AQE dynamically handles skew in sort merge join and shuffle hash join by splitting and replicating skewed tasks into roughly evenly sized tasks.

plausible_options.B: one task in a groupBy stage reading 50 GB of shuffle data

eliminated_by.C: The fix must spread that one hot key over more tasks
eliminated_by.D: Adaptive Query Execution is on and the stage is an aggregation, not a join

distractor_traps.B: T5: common misconception - more memory lets one oversized task survive but never rebalances the key
distractor_traps.C: T2: scope error - fewer partitions concentrate the hot key further instead of spreading it
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - disabling AQE does not turn an aggregation into a broadcast

stem: A daily ETL job finished in 45 minutes today after finishing in 12 minutes for the past month. The on-call engineer must first establish how today's duration compares with earlier runs of the same job.

option_texts.A: Open the task graph to confirm every downstream task was scheduled in the right order
option_texts.B: Open the workspace file browser and compare the input file sizes against yesterday
option_texts.C: Open the job's run history and read how long previous runs of this job took
option_texts.D: Open the Spark UI metrics tab and read stage-level shuffle and memory counters

drill_answer_short: Run history retains prior runs and their total running time, which is what a baseline comparison needs
decision_hinge: Databricks retains run history for 60 days for both jobs and pipelines, and the matrix view displays the run's total duration and the run's state for each run.

plausible_options.D: A daily ETL job finished in 45 minutes today

eliminated_by.A: must first establish how today's duration compares with earlier runs
eliminated_by.B: after finishing in 12 minutes for the past month

distractor_traps.A: T2: scope error - task ordering explains a wrong result, not a slower run against its own history
distractor_traps.B: T2: scope error - input size is a candidate cause, but it is not where the baseline comparison lives
distractor_traps.D: T3: confusable sibling - the Spark UI explains why one run was slow, after history establishes that it was

stem: A Lakeflow Job cannot start because its classic compute never reaches a running state. The job definition is unchanged and ran yesterday, so the team must look at the compute lifecycle itself rather than at anything the job code did.

option_texts.A: Open the Spark UI on that compute and look for out-of-memory errors and failed tasks
option_texts.B: Open the compute Event log tab to read the lifecycle events behind the failed start
option_texts.C: Open the job run history and wait to see whether a later retry eventually succeeds
option_texts.D: Open the job task graph and find the upstream task meant to drive the compute lifecycle

drill_answer_short: Compute event logs capture lifecycle events such as creation and termination, and are read from the Event log tab
decision_hinge: Compute event logs capture compute lifecycle events like creation, termination, and configuration edits, and to view the compute's event log you select the Event log tab on the compute details pages.

plausible_options.A: its classic compute never reaches a running state

eliminated_by.C: the team must look at the compute lifecycle itself
eliminated_by.D: The job definition is unchanged and ran yesterday

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - the Spark UI needs a compute that already started, which is the thing that failed
distractor_traps.C: T2: scope error - waiting on a retry observes the symptom instead of diagnosing the start
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - no upstream task creates the compute for a job run

stem: A stage spills large amounts of data to disk because each post-shuffle partition is too big to sit in memory. The team is choosing one setting to change first, and the cluster already runs with Adaptive Query Execution enabled.

option_texts.A: Raise spark.sql.shuffle.partitions so each post-shuffle partition holds less data
option_texts.B: Lower spark.sql.shuffle.partitions so the stage runs fewer, larger shuffle reads
option_texts.C: Shrink the cluster so each post-shuffle partition is packed more tightly in memory
option_texts.D: Switch the table to liquid clustering so the layout removes the spilling

drill_answer_short: Spill means each partition is oversized, so raise the shuffle partition count to put less data in each one
decision_hinge: A plan built on wrong estimates might create too many small tasks after a shuffle, or create a few oversized tasks that hold up the whole stage, and AQE picks an optimal number and size of post-shuffle partitions.

plausible_options.B: The team is choosing one setting to change first

eliminated_by.C: each post-shuffle partition is too big to sit in memory
eliminated_by.D: A stage spills large amounts of data to disk

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - fewer partitions is the right move for tiny tasks and the wrong one for oversized tasks
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated - less memory cannot make an oversized partition fit
distractor_traps.D: T2: scope error - clustering changes the table layout and not the size of a shuffle partition

stem: A large Delta table is updated and queried constantly, and queries filter on customer_id. The team wants a layout that it can re-key later without rewriting the table by hand, and it does not want to maintain fixed partitions.

option_texts.A: Define a static partition on customer_id so the files are organised by that range
option_texts.B: Turn on predictive optimization so OPTIMIZE and VACUUM run on a managed schedule
option_texts.C: Apply ZORDER BY customer_id and schedule a weekly OPTIMIZE to keep the layout fresh
option_texts.D: Enable liquid clustering on customer_id, which replaces partitioning and ZORDER and can be re-keyed later

drill_answer_short: Liquid clustering replaces partitioning and ZORDER, and its clustering keys can be changed at any time
decision_hinge: Liquid clustering is a data layout optimization technique that replaces table partitioning and ZORDER, and you can change clustering keys for a table at any time.

plausible_options.C: The team wants a layout that it can re-key later without rewriting the table by hand

eliminated_by.A: it does not want to maintain fixed partitions

distractor_traps.A: T4: breaks a stated requirement - a static partition is the fixed partitioning the team ruled out
distractor_traps.B: T2: scope error - predictive optimization schedules maintenance and does not choose the layout
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - ZORDER does co-locate the column, but changing the ordering means rewriting the layout by hand
